title: Under-Cabinet Lighting Upgrade: LED Fixtures, Centralized Switch, and USB Outlet

locations.name: Probable kitchen
locations.basis: Transcript mentions cooktop and cooking activities, implying a kitchen setting

summary: This video documents a retrofit of under-cabinet lighting from an aging fluorescent setup to LED diode-based fixtures, with a single centralized switch and a new USB-enabled outlet strip. The presenters compare old and new fixtures, relocate wiring into an in-cabinet box, and route power from the panel to the front of the cabinets. They demonstrate wiring the switch (hot, switched hot, neutral, and ground), using push-in connectors, daisy-chaining fixtures with a joiner, and installing a USB outlet strip under the cabinets. The result is a brighter, clutter-free counter space with easier control, plus a dimmer for LED lighting and a built-in tablet charging option.

sections.title: Context, problems, and plan for upgrade
concepts: desire to consolidate to a single switch
sections.description: The hosts discuss the downsides of the current two-light setup and countertop outlets, praising a mounted plug strip but noting its forward position. They outline the plan to relocate the strip, extend it to the edge, and install a new LED fixture arrangement that provides full countertop coverage with a single wall switch.

sections.description: The old fixture is introduced and the LED replacement is described as diode-based with no bulbs. They plan to move wiring into an in-cabinet box to accommodate a single switched circuit and reroute power to front-facing fixtures, including eliminating the old wiring at the back of the cabinet.

sections.title: Installation, connections, and testing
concepts: switch wiring: hot black, switched hot red, neutral white, ground
final power-on test and tablet charging
sections.description: Wiring the wall switch is demonstrated, including a new conductor to feed the lights from a single switch. The fixtures connect with push-in connectors, and a joiner supplies power along the chain. A USB-equipped outlet strip is installed under the cabinet, connected from the panel, and a dimmer is used to control the LEDs. The segment ends with restoring power and testing the improved brightness and charging capability.
